prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1188; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is not named on the policy and does not live with the policyholder.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a low-speed head-on collision. The claimant reports neck pain and is represented by counsel, who has asked that all contact go through their office.

Entry 2: Police report, photographs and statements from the other driver and two independent witnesses all describe the collision as the claimant has described it. The claimant is confirmed as a passenger in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 3: Repair estimate matches the impact pattern shown in the photographs. Vehicle history shows no prior damage claims, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known from inspection.

Entry 4: The claimant's account has stayed consistent across the first statement, the recorded interview and the written submission. The injury description fits the force of the impact. Medical records show a prior minor strain in the same area that resolved fully some years ago.

Entry 5: Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, and the physiotherapy schedule is being reviewed against standard recovery timelines. A neighbor has told the field adjuster they believe the car was already damaged some weeks before the claimed date, but this has not been confirmed by any other source.

Entry 6: The driver at the time of loss is not named on the policy and does not live with the policyholder, so the permissive use question is being checked against the policy terms. Referred to the supervisor for review of coverage and the treatment timeline before any settlement offer is made.
